name: Oregon
summary: Navy blue with gold lettering 'STATE OF OREGON' and '1859' around the state escutcheon on the front, and a gold beaver on the reverse. It is the only US state flag with different designs on each side.
origin: The flag was adopted on 26 February 1925. 1859 is the year Oregon became the 33rd state.

symbols.name: Escutcheon
symbols.description: A shield with mountains, forests, an elk, a covered wagon, the ocean with a departing British ship and an arriving American ship, a plough, sheaves and a pickaxe, under an eagle.
symbols.meaning: Oregon's landscape, settlement and industry; the ships show the end of British influence.

symbols.name: Beaver (reverse)
symbols.meaning: The state animal; Oregon is the Beaver State, from its fur-trading history.

facts: It is the only US state flag with a different design on the reverse.
Paraguay is the only national flag with different sides.
The beaver honours Oregon's fur-trapping history.
clues: Navy blue with gold 'STATE OF OREGON' and a shield on the front, and a beaver on the back.
The only US state flag with two different sides.
